title: Rethinking the Bounds of LLM Reasoning: Are Multi-Agent Discussions the Key?
authors: Qineng Wang, Zihao Wang, Ying Su, Hanghang Tong, Yangqiu Song
venue: Proceedings of ACL 2024 (Vol. 1: Long Papers), pp. 6106-6131
metadata_verified_via: ACL Anthology (earlier verified note) + arXiv HTML v1
objective: Test whether multi-agent discussion beats a single agent with strong prompts on reasoning
architecture_methods: Debate (3/6 agents), MAD (3), ReConcile (multi-LLM), proposed CMD group discussion (6); max 3 rounds; Direct vs Demo prompting
dataset_sample: ECQA (100), GSM8K (100), FOLIO-wiki (460)
main_findings: ChatGPT-3.5 averages (Direct/Demo): single 67.41/75.63; MAD(3) 63.42/70.04; Debate(3) 71.67/73.88; CMD(6) 70.75/74.46. Multi-agent wins only without demonstrations; with demos single agent highest average. Multi-LLM CMD 76.93/78.66 vs single Gemini Pro 74.38/78.59. Error types: Judge Mistake, Wrong Answer Propagation.
limitations: Small samples (100 items for 2 tasks); older models; no token/cost reporting; non-medical
relevance: P4/RQ4 - strong prompted single agent nearly matches multi-agent; baselines must be strong
supports_or_contradicts: Challenges multi-agent premise; supports need for strong single-agent baselines
claims_supported: Single agent with strong prompts ~ best multi-agent discussion; MA helps only without demonstrations

title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
authors: Andries Smit, Nathan Grinsztajn, Paul Duckworth, Thomas D. Barrett, Arnu Pretorius
published_version_checked: yes - ICML 2024 (arXiv 2311.17371; v1 titled 'Are we going MAD? Benchmarking Multi-Agent Debate between Language Models for Medical Q&A')
metadata_verified_via: PMLR page (earlier verified note); arXiv HTML v3; ICML virtual page in search results
objective: Benchmark MAD protocols against other prompting strategies on accuracy, cost and time
architecture_methods: Society of Minds, Multi-Persona, ChatEval variants, Ensemble Refinement; agreement-intensity modulation
models_tools: GPT-3.5-turbo; GPT-4 and Mixtral 8x7B on MedQA
dataset_sample: MedQA 4-option (1,273), PubMedQA (500), MMLU clinical (123), CosmosQA (500), CIAR (50), GPQA (448), Chess
main_findings: MAD does not reliably outperform self-consistency and ensembling. MedQA Table 2 best/median: Medprompt 0.65/0.63; SoM 0.64/0.61; ER 0.64/0.60; Self-Consistency 0.60/0.60; Single Agent 0.60/0.59; Multi-Persona 0.58/0.57 (extraction flagged inconsistency with text/Table 3 - verify). On medical datasets all systems except Multi-Persona beat single-agent methods; on non-medical, single-agent methods beat all except Multi-Persona and SC. Agreement modulation: ~+15% Multi-Persona, ~+5% SoM on 376-question USMLE subset. MedQA cost: SoM ~$1.73-$5.19 vs ~$2.16 Medprompt/SC.
limitations: Mainly GPT-3.5; hyperparameter sensitivity; some internal numeric inconsistency in extraction
relevance: P4/RQ4 - medical QA; MAD vs SC/ensembles with cost; tuning sensitivity
supports_or_contradicts: Challenges multi-agent premise (not reliably better than SC); partial support on medical datasets vs plain single agent
claims_supported: MAD not reliably better than SC/ensembling; MAD hyperparameter-sensitive; cost must be reported

title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
authors: Yilun Du, Shuang Li, Antonio Torralba, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Igor Mordatch
objective: Improve reasoning and factuality via multiple LLM instances debating over rounds
architecture_methods: Multiagent debate (society of minds), same prompts across tasks, black-box models
main_findings: Abstract reports improved mathematical and strategic reasoning, improved factual validity and reduced hallucinations. No numbers extracted this session.
limitations: Full text not read; Huang et al. 2024 show its debate underperforms self-consistency at equal responses on full GSM8K
relevance: P4/RQ4 - foundational pro-multi-agent claim being tested
supports_or_contradicts: Supports multi-agent premise (against weaker baselines)
claims_supported: Debate improves reasoning/factuality vs single instance

title: Encouraging Divergent Thinking in Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Tian Liang, Zhiwei He, Wenxiang Jiao, Xing Wang, Yan Wang, Rui Wang, Yujiu Yang, Shuming Shi, Zhaopeng Tu
objective: Address Degeneration-of-Thought in self-reflection via adversarial debate with a judge
architecture_methods: MAD: debaters argue 'tit for tat', judge decides; adaptive break
dataset_sample: Commonsense machine translation; counter-intuitive arithmetic reasoning
main_findings: Abstract: MAD effective on both tasks; adaptive break of debate and modest 'tit for tat' needed; LLM judge may not be fair when debaters are different LLMs. No numbers extracted.
limitations: Full text not read; Wang et al. ACL 2024 found MAD(3) below single agent on average
relevance: P4/RQ4 - foundational MAD; judge bias failure mode
supports_or_contradicts: Supports multi-agent premise; also documents judge fairness issue
claims_supported: Degeneration-of-Thought; judge bias

title: More Agents Is All You Need
authors: Junyou Li, Qin Zhang, Yangbin Yu, Qiang Fu, Deheng Ye
metadata_verified_via: mlanthology TMLR record; arXiv HTML v2
objective: Show LLM performance scales with number of sampled agents via sampling-and-voting
architecture_methods: Agent Forest: sample N, majority vote; combinable with CoT, SPP, Debate, Reflexion
dataset_sample: GSM8K, MATH, Chess state tracking, MMLU, HumanEval; ensemble up to 40; 10 runs
baselines: CoT, zero-shot CoT, SPP, LLM-Debate, Reflexion
main_findings: Single->40 agents: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 0.73->0.85, MATH 0.29->0.39, MMLU 0.59->0.70; Llama2-13B GSM8K 0.35->0.59 (> Llama2-70B single 0.54). Gains larger on harder tasks (MATH rel. +200% Llama2-13B). Standalone beats Debate/Reflexion in most cases; avg rank Ours 2.5 vs Debate 4.4. Token use ~proportional to ensemble size.
limitations: Cost not optimised; MCQ/short-answer tasks; non-medical
relevance: RQ4/P4 - number of calls is a performance lever; compute confound
supports_or_contradicts: Challenges attributing gains to agent interaction; supports compute-matched SC baseline
claims_supported: Sampling-and-voting scales with N and rivals complex multi-agent methods

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
authors: Xuezhi Wang, Jason Wei, Dale Schuurmans, Quoc Le, Ed Chi, Sharan Narang, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Denny Zhou
published_version_checked: yes - ICLR 2023 (from ICLR virtual listing in search results; not opened)
metadata_verified_via: arXiv abs page; ICLR 2023 virtual listing (search result)
objective: Replace greedy CoT decoding with sampling diverse paths and majority answer
architecture_methods: Self-consistency decoding
dataset_sample: GSM8K, SVAMP, AQuA, StrategyQA, ARC-challenge
main_findings: Gains over CoT: GSM8K +17.9%, SVAMP +11.0%, AQuA +12.2%, StrategyQA +6.4%, ARC-challenge +3.9%.
limitations: Abstract only; models not extracted
relevance: RQ4 - canonical compute-matched single-agent baseline
supports_or_contradicts: Supports compute confound explanation

title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
authors: Jie Huang et al.
published_version_checked: yes - ICLR 2024 (virtual poster listing in search results; arXiv 2310.01798)
metadata_verified_via: arXiv HTML v2; ICLR 2024 virtual listing (search result)
objective: Test intrinsic self-correction and multi-agent debate without oracle feedback
architecture_methods: Intrinsic self-correction; multi-agent debate (3 agents, 2 rounds, Du et al. prompts) vs self-consistency at equal responses
dataset_sample: Full GSM8K test; CommonSenseQA; HotpotQA
baselines: Standard prompting; self-consistency at 3/6/9 responses; oracle-guided correction
main_findings: GSM8K: debate 83.2 (6 responses) vs SC 85.3 (6); debate 83.0 (9) vs SC 88.2 (9); standard 76.7. Intrinsic self-correction GPT-3.5: GSM8K 75.9->74.7, CSQA 75.8->41.8, HotpotQA 26.0->25.0. Prior gains relied on oracle labels.
limitations: One model in debate section; first author only recorded (full list not verified)
relevance: RQ4/P4 - direct equal-response comparison; cost analysis call
supports_or_contradicts: Contradicts multi-agent debate superiority at matched responses
claims_supported: Debate < SC at equal responses; self-correction without oracle hurts

title: Are More LLM Calls All You Need? Towards the Scaling Properties of Compound AI Systems
authors: Lingjiao Chen, Jared Quincy Davis, Boris Hanin, Peter Bailis, Ion Stoica, Matei Zaharia, James Zou
objective: Characterise how performance of Vote / Filter-Vote scales with number of LM calls
architecture_methods: Vote, Filter-Vote; analytical scaling model
dataset_sample: Multiple language tasks
main_findings: Performance can first increase then decrease with more calls (non-monotonic); more calls help easy queries and hurt hard ones; optimal call number predictable from few samples.
limitations: Abstract only; numbers not extracted
relevance: RQ4 - compute budget must be swept; more compute not monotone
supports_or_contradicts: Nuances compute confound (more calls not always better)
claims_supported: Non-monotonic scaling of voting with calls

title: Debate or Vote: Which Yields Better Decisions in Multi-Agent Large Language Models?
authors: Hyeong Kyu Choi, Xiaojin (Jerry) Zhu, Sharon Li
metadata_verified_via: NeurIPS 2025 virtual page; arXiv HTML v2
objective: Disentangle majority voting from inter-agent debate in MAD
architecture_methods: Decentralized/Sparse/Centralized MAD vs majority voting; DCM Bayesian model; martingale theorem; MAD-Conformist/Follower
dataset_sample: Arithmetics, GSM8K, MMLU Prof. Medicine, MMLU Formal Logic, HellaSwag, CommonsenseQA, HH-RLHF; N=5, T=2/3/5
main_findings: Qwen2.5-7B avg: majority vote 0.7691; decentralized MAD 0.7377/0.7112/0.7050 (T=2/3/5); centralized 0.6551-0.6672; single 0.7205. Llama3.1-8B: vote 0.7242; MAD 0.6929-0.6761; single 0.6203. Debate belief is a martingale (no expected improvement). MAD-oracle 0.7084->0.8289; MAD-Conformist/Follower ~0.75-0.76.
limitations: Small open models; MCQ-style; no token cost figures in part read
relevance: RQ4/P4 - voting explains MAD gains; includes medical MMLU subset
supports_or_contradicts: Contradicts debate-specific benefit
claims_supported: Majority voting accounts for most MAD gains

title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
authors: Hangfan Zhang, Zhiyao Cui, Jianhao Chen, Xinrun Wang, Qiaosheng Zhang, Zhen Wang, Dinghao Wu, Shuyue Hu
published_version_checked: no venue found on arXiv page
objective: Systematically evaluate MAD against simple single-agent baselines
architecture_methods: 5 MAD methods
dataset_sample: 9 benchmarks
main_findings: MAD often fails to outperform CoT and SC even with significantly more inference-time compute; model heterogeneity consistently improves MAD. No numbers seen.
limitations: Abstract only
relevance: P4/RQ4 - evaluation flaws: limited benchmarks, weak baselines, inconsistent setups
supports_or_contradicts: Challenges multi-agent premise; heterogeneity as moderator

title: Talk Isn't Always Cheap: Understanding Failure Modes in Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Andrea Wynn, Harsh Satija, Gillian K. Hadfield
objective: Identify when and why debate lowers accuracy
architecture_methods: 2-round debate, majority vote final; homogeneous and mixed-capability groups
dataset_sample: CommonSenseQA, MMLU, GSM8K; 100 samples each; 5 seeds
main_findings: 3xMistral MMLU 33.6->24.4; 1 LLaMA+2 Mistral MMLU 40.0->28.0; all configs declined on CSQA; diverse group MMLU 57.8->63.4, GSM8K 86.8->90.2. Correct->incorrect flips outnumber incorrect->correct; social pressure/conformity; correctness-payoff prompt did not reduce flips.
limitations: 100 items per task; small models
relevance: RQ4/RQ1 - conformity failure mode; debate can lower accuracy
supports_or_contradicts: Challenges debate premise; heterogeneity sometimes helps
claims_supported: Debate can degrade accuracy via conformity

title: Peacemaker or Troublemaker: How Sycophancy Shapes Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Binwei Yao, Chao Shang, Wanyu Du, Jianfeng He, Ruixue Lian, Yi Zhang, Hang Su, Sandesh Swamy, Yanjun Qi
objective: Quantify how sycophancy affects MAD
architecture_methods: Decentralized SoM and centralized judge debate; sycophancy levels 1-8 via prompts; 2-3 agents; 5 rounds (AutoGen)
models_tools: Qwen3-32B, LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct; GPT-5-mini as judge of sycophancy score
dataset_sample: MMLU-Pro (1,000), CommonsenseQA validation
metrics: Accuracy; Disagreement Collapse Rate; Negative Agreement Rate; Sycophancy Score
main_findings: Decentralized DCR 81.71% (Qwen-Qwen), 86.36% (Llama-Llama) on CSQA; centralized judge 41.27%/35.51%. NAR vs SS r=0.902. Decentralized debate below single agent (CSQA 83.62% vs 85.50%). Suggest cap 2-3 exchanges.
limitations: Two models, two benchmarks, two frameworks
relevance: RQ4 - sycophancy failure mode; centralized judge more resilient
supports_or_contradicts: Challenges decentralized debate; supports centralized structure
claims_supported: Sycophancy drives disagreement collapse

title: The Cost of Consensus: Isolated Self-Correction Prevails Over Unguided Homogeneous Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Blaž Bertalanič, Carolina Fortuna
objective: Compare homogeneous MAD vs isolated self-correction under matched agents/rounds
architecture_methods: N=10 identical agents, R=3, full connectivity, plurality vote; noise-injection controls
dataset_sample: GSM-Hard (1,017 for Qwen; 100 otherwise), MMLU-Hard STEM (100)
baselines: Isolated self-correction; single agent with 10x output budget
main_findings: Debate never beat self-correction: GSM-Hard Ministral 20.7% vs 48.3%; MMLU-Hard Qwen 60.7% vs 66.7%; debate used 2.1-3.4x more tokens. Modal sycophancy up to 85.5%; oracle gap up to 32.3 pts.
limitations: 7-8B models; 100-item subsets; tokens not matched; Llama differences n.s.
relevance: RQ4 - cost-accuracy; conformity
supports_or_contradicts: Contradicts homogeneous debate benefit
claims_supported: Isolated self-correction better cost-accuracy than homogeneous debate

title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
authors: Yubin Kim, Ken Gu, Chanwoo Park, Chunjong Park, Samuel Schmidgall, A. Ali Heydari, Yao Yan, Zhihan Zhang, Yuchen Zhuang, Yun Liu, Mark Malhotra, Paul Pu Liang, Hae Won Park, Yuzhe Yang, Xuhai Xu, Yilun Du, Shwetak Patel, Tim Althoff, Daniel McDuff, Xin Liu
published_version_checked: no venue listed on arXiv v3
metadata_verified_via: arXiv abs page v3; arXiv HTML
objective: Derive principles predicting when multi-agent coordination helps
architecture_methods: Single-agent vs independent, centralized, decentralized, hybrid MAS; identical prompts, tools and budgets (stated); mixed-effects regression
dataset_sample: 260 configurations; BrowseComp-Plus, Finance-Agent, PlanCraft, WorkBench, SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench
main_findings: +80.8% (centralized, decomposable finance) to -70.0% (sequential planning); all MAS degrade planning 39-70%; negative returns above ~45% single-agent accuracy (beta=-0.236, p=0.004); tool-coordination trade-off beta=-0.096, p=0.002; error amplification 17.2x independent vs 4.4x centralized; CV R^2=0.373; best architecture for 87% held-out configs.
limitations: No healthcare benchmark; modest explained variance; budget protocol (Appendix E) not read
relevance: RQ4/P4 - matched-budget architecture comparison; centralized verification
supports_or_contradicts: Conditional: supports centralized MAS on decomposable tasks; contradicts MAS for sequential/tool-heavy/strong baselines
claims_supported: Capability saturation; tool overhead; centralized coordination limits errors

title: When Single-Agent with Skills Replace Multi-Agent Systems and When They Fail
authors: Xiaoxiao Li
objective: Test whether a single agent with a skill library can replace MAS and where skill selection breaks
architecture_methods: MAS-to-SAS compilation (capability decomposition, backend assignment, topology internalization); skill library scaling 5-200
dataset_sample: GSM8K, HumanEval, HotpotQA
main_findings: Skill-based single agent matched MAS accuracy with 54% fewer tokens and 50% lower latency on average (preliminary). Skill selection shows phase transition with library size driven by semantic confusability; hierarchical routing mitigates. Debate, parallel sampling, private info, heterogeneous agents not compilable.
limitations: Preliminary; small libraries; single author list as extracted; exact numbers not seen
relevance: RQ4 - single-agent-with-tools baseline at lower cost
supports_or_contradicts: Challenges need for MAS when roles are serializable (as in pipeline designs)
claims_supported: Single agent with skills matches MAS at lower cost

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
authors: Mert Cemri, Melissa Z. Pan, Shuyi Yang, Lakshya A. Agrawal, Bhavya Chopra, Rishabh Tiwari, Kurt Keutzer, Aditya Parameswaran, Dan Klein, Kannan Ramchandran, Matei Zaharia, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Ion Stoica
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (spotlight poster; track not stated on page)
objective: Systematically characterise MAS failures
architecture_methods: Grounded-theory taxonomy (MAST) from traces; LLM-as-judge annotator
models_tools: GPT-4, Claude 3, Qwen2.5, CodeLlama; 7 MAS frameworks
dataset_sample: 150 traces for taxonomy; MAST-Data 1,600+ traces; coding, math, general agent tasks
main_findings: MAS gains on popular benchmarks 'often minimal'; 14 failure modes in 3 categories (system design issues, inter-agent misalignment, task verification); kappa=0.88.

title: AI Agents That Matter
authors: Sayash Kapoor, Benedikt Stroebl, Zachary S. Siegel, Nitya Nadgir, Arvind Narayanan
metadata_verified_via: mlanthology TMLR record; arXiv HTML v1
objective: Critique agent benchmarking and propose cost-aware, reproducible evaluation
architecture_methods: Simple baselines (retry, warming, escalation) vs complex agents; Pareto frontier; joint accuracy-cost optimisation; holdout analysis
dataset_sample: HumanEval (164, 5 runs); HotPotQA; WebArena, NovelQA analysis
main_findings: HumanEval: Warming 93.2% $2.45; Retry 92.0% $2.51; Reflexion 87.8% $3.90; LATS(GPT-4) 88.0% $134.50; LDB+Reflexion 92.9% $7.26. Joint optimisation ~53% (GPT-3.5) and ~41% (Llama-3-70B) lower cost on HotPotQA. Appropriate holdouts: 1/1, 3/6, 1/8, 0/2 by generality level. Reproduced accuracies often below reported; error bars rare.
limitations: Prices change over time; coding/QA focus
relevance: RQ4/P4 - cost-accuracy Pareto, holdouts, reproducibility
supports_or_contradicts: Challenges complex agent designs without simple baselines
claims_supported: Report cost and tokens; simple baselines; holdouts; CIs

title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
authors: Sayash Kapoor, Benedikt Stroebl, Peter Kirgis, et al. (31 authors) ... Percy Liang, Arvind Narayanan
objective: Standardised, cost-aware, multi-dimensional agent evaluation infrastructure
architecture_methods: Parallel harness across VMs; models x scaffolds x benchmarks analysis; LLM-aided log inspection
dataset_sample: 21,730 rollouts; 9 benchmarks (coding, web navigation, science, customer service); ~$40,000; 2.5B tokens of logs
main_findings: Higher reasoning effort reduced accuracy in the majority of runs; logs revealed agents searching for benchmark on HuggingFace and misusing credit cards; evaluation time weeks->hours.
limitations: Abstract only this session
relevance: RQ4 - cost reporting, log inspection, reasoning-effort confound
supports_or_contradicts: Methodological; longer reasoning not reliably better
claims_supported: Standardised harness; cost-aware evaluation

title: MedAgentBoard: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration with Conventional Methods for Diverse Medical Tasks
authors: Yinghao Zhu, Ziyi He, Haoran Hu, Xiaochen Zheng, Xichen Zhang, Zixiang Wang, Junyi Gao, Liantao Ma, Lequan Yu

title: MedAgentsBench: Benchmarking Thinking Models and Agent Frameworks for Complex Medical Reasoning
authors: Xiangru Tang, Daniel Shao, Jiwoong Sohn, Jiapeng Chen, Jiayi Zhang, Jinyu Xiang, Fang Wu, Yilun Zhao, Chenglin Wu, Wenqi Shi, Arman Cohan, Mark Gerstein
objective: Benchmark thinking models vs agent frameworks on hard medical questions incl. cost
architecture_methods: Prompting (zero/few-shot, CoT, CoT-SC, MultiPersona, Self-Refine, MedPrompt) and agent frameworks (MedAgents, MDAgents, AFlow, SPO)
models_tools: DeepSeek-R1, o3-mini, o1-mini, QwQ-32B, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5 Sonnet/Haiku, DeepSeek-V3, Llama-3.3-70B

main_findings: Thinking models (DeepSeek-R1, o3-mini) best and on Pareto frontier; GPT-4o HARD avg: CoT 24.3%, CoT-SC 25.3%, MedAgents 20.0%, MDAgents 16.1%, AFlow 28.9%. Agent frameworks not consistently better and heavier overhead. Total experiment cost $226.17.

title: MedAgentAudit: Diagnosing and Quantifying Collaborative Failure Modes in Medical Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Lei Gu, Yinghao Zhu, Haoran Sang, Zixiang Wang, Dehao Sui, Wen Tang, Ewen Harrison, Junyi Gao, Lequan Yu, Liantao Ma
objective: Audit collaboration processes and failure modes of medical MAS
architecture_methods: Log annotation taxonomy (4 phases); quantitative process metrics
models_tools: ColaCare, ReConcile, MDAgents, MedAgents, MAC, HealthcareAgent
dataset_sample: 3,600 logs; MedQA, PubMedQA, MedXpertQA, PathVQA, VQA-RAD, SLAKE
metrics: Failure shares; key-evidence-unit missing rate; clinical priority mismatch; voting reliance; conflict dropout; kappa
main_findings: Flawed consensus 19.7%; incorrect knowledge 13.5%; minority suppression 5.9%; 68.6% of successes superfluous collaboration; minority correction ~10%; KEU missing 11.23%-62.92%; priority mismatch 72.16%-84.18%; voting over evidence up to 46.46% (ColaCare); kappa 0.82.
limitations: MCQ/VQA datasets; no single-agent arm
relevance: RQ1/RQ2/RQ4 - medical MAS failure modes (false consensus, information loss, risk prioritisation)
supports_or_contradicts: Challenges MAS robustness in medicine; supports deterministic decision core and red-flag rules
claims_supported: Medical MAS favour conformity over correction

title: The Optimization Paradox in Clinical AI Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Suhana Bedi, Iddah Mlauzi, Daniel Shin, Sanmi Koyejo, Nigam H. Shah
objective: Compare single vs multi-agent and component-optimised systems on real clinical cases
architecture_methods: Information gathering / interpretation / differential diagnosis stages; 8 single-agent, 26 multi-agent systems; Best-of-Breed assembly
dataset_sample: MIMIC-CDM, 2,400 ED cases (appendicitis 957, pancreatitis 538, cholecystitis 648, diverticulitis 257); 1,190 dev / 1,190 test
metrics: Diagnostic accuracy; process metrics; computational and lab cost; McNemar
main_findings: MAS win rate: info gathering 78.4% (p=0.015), interpretation 87.5% (p=0.0008), computational cost 76.9% (p=0.022); diagnostic accuracy 52.9% n.s. Top MAS 77.39% vs top single 75.63%; BoB 67.65% (-9.75 pts vs top MAS, McNemar p<0.0001); BoB hallucinated test results 13.87% vs 0.42%.
limitations: Single centre; 4 abdominal pathologies; basic orchestration; compute matching not established
relevance: RQ1/RQ4/P4 - real-data single vs multi; component vs end-to-end
supports_or_contradicts: No diagnostic advantage for MAS (challenges premise); MAS better on process
claims_supported: Component optimisation does not predict system performance

title: Do Mixed-Vendor Multi-Agent LLMs Improve Clinical Diagnosis?
authors: Grace Chang Yuan, Xiaoman Zhang, Sung Eun Kim, Pranav Rajpurkar
objective: Test whether vendor diversity in MAC improves diagnosis over single LLMs and single-vendor teams
architecture_methods: MAC: 3 doctor agents + supervisor, round-robin, max 13 turns; single-LLM, single-vendor, mixed-vendor
models_tools: o4-mini, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-4.5-Sonnet; o4-mini judge; BioLORD check
dataset_sample: RareBench MME 40, HMS 88, LIRICAL 370; DiagnosisArena 165
main_findings: Combined RareBench R@1: best single 37.58, best single-vendor MAC 33.32, mixed 39.31; DiagnosisArena Top-1: OpenAI single 32.12%, mixed 36.36%. Single-vendor teams can underperform base model; 'consensus trap'.
limitations: Small subsets; single runs; no significance tests; judge is a tested model; compute not controlled
relevance: RQ4 - heterogeneity as moderator in clinical diagnosis
supports_or_contradicts: Supports MA only with vendor diversity; homogeneous teams can hurt
claims_supported: Mixed-vendor MA > single LLM (unmatched compute)
